newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-W.Australia wants value added nickel industry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-W.Australia wants value added nickel industry.

text.p: The A$1.1 billion Western Australian nickel industry should consider value-adding opportunities, such as an export-oriented stainless steel plant, State Resources Minister Colin Barnett said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the Nickel 96 conference Kalgoorlie, Barnett said the Western Australian nickel industry would continue to strengthen and with this positive outlet producers must look towards downstream processing opportunities.
Western Australia currently produced 11 percent of the world's nickel, with production of 101,000 tonnes of nickel in concentrates in 1995, he said.

"The value of Western Australian nickel production now exceeds A$1.1 billion with the industry and its commentators predicting a period of sustained growth through to the year 2000 and beyond," Barnett said.
A copy of his speech was released here.

"With increasing nickel production in WA and the deregulation of the energy industry providing lower prices, it is appropriate that the industry looks seriously at further value adding to see if we can do better than just converting to nickel metal," Barnett said.
